title: Cross-arch quant SLA playbook
summary: Playbook and experimental notes for benchmarking quantized model variants (INT8 / AWQ / GPTQ / FP8) across multiple GPU architectures with the goal of defining safe rollout gates and automated fallback rules for SLA preservation.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic playbook for evaluating quantized model variants across different accelerator architectures (A100, H100, L4) and kernel implementations. The goal: produce reproducible signals that map to clear rollout gates (latency, p95 tail, throughput per-dollar, and a small set of quality checks) so that the control plane can automatically choose safe defaults and fallback strategies when serving.
notes: This is a working doc — contains partial results, hypotheses, and the test harness config we used in June 2027. Final numbers should be migrated to the /bench-results bucket and to the Confluence page above.
Background: We frequently see model-variant behavior change depending on: kernel selection, sequence-length distribution, KV cache pressure, and accelerator memory layout. Past incidents (see INF-2412) showed that an INT8 kernel optimized for throughput on H100 introduced >2x p95 tail for short-chat workloads when batching increased. This playbook documents a controlled approach to detect and mitigate those regressions before wide rollout.
Testbed and harness:
Hardware: A100-40GB (PCIe), H100-80GB, and Nvidia L4 (48GB).
Software: serving-runtime main@commit: 0d9f3a; custom kernel builds (vector-lane-v2, cuBLAS-fallback).
Models: open-compiler v1.3 (base-7b), and a tuned 13b candiate.
Quant variants: FP16 baseline, INT8-GPTQ, INT8-AWQ (4-bit AWQ not covered here), FP8-experimental.
Workloads: 1) Short-chat mix (avg 12 tokens request, 8 decode); 2) Long-context summarization (avg 800 tokens context, 256 decode); 3) Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) hot-path with frequent KV eviction.
Harness: continuous client-sim that replays production-like inter-arrival distributions. Each run collects p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, OOM events, memory footprint, and quality checks (perplexity on held set + 200 prompt QA accuracy samples).
Run policy: 3 cold-start runs and 10 steady-state ramped runs per config per instance type.
Artifact: harness config stored as a standalone YAML (linked in PR #7821).
Metrics and gates:
Primary metrics: p95 decode latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), numeric quality delta (relative perplexity increase and QA accuracy drop). Secondary: memory headroom, tail jitter (p99/p95 ratio), and GPU kernel occupancy.
Suggested rollout gates (initial):
- p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.2 (<=20% increase) for short-chat workload at 95% of target throughput.
- QA accuracy drop <= 1.5 percentage points on the QA sample set.
- No sustained OOMs or kernel-fatal errors.
- Throughput per-dollar improvement >= 10% vs baseline, or latency improvement to justify quality tradeoff.
If any gate fails, automatic routing should prefer FP16 baseline or a verified fallback kernel for that architecture.
Key experimental observations:
1) Kernel sensitivity vs seq length: vector-lane-v2 shows strong throughput wins for short-chat on H100 with AWQ but exhibits higher p95 variance under bursty arrival patterns.
2) Memory layout differences: A100 with older PCIe drivers thrashes the KV cache at ~700 token context for INT8-GPTQ causing periodic p99 spikes; H100 maintained steadier ordering.
3) FP8 behavior: FP8-experimental matched INT8 throughput on L4 for long-context but had a ~0.9 point QA accuracy regression on the summarization set — borderline for rollout.
4) AWQ benefits: AWQ provided best tokens/sec on H100 for base-7b but quality on edge-case prompts (numeric reasoning style) degraded compared to GPTQ by ~2.2% relative accuracy.
5) Decoder interaction: sampling top-k=40 + temperature 0.8 increased tail latency variability by ~18% compared to greedy; quant kernels amplify this effect because decoding kernels are less predictable in memory access patterns.
6) Kernel fallback cost: enabling cuBLAS-fallback reduces p95 tail but cut throughput by ~12% on H100; useful as an automated fallback during detected jitter windows.
Representative numbers (short-chat, avg:
Baseline FP16 on H100: p95=82ms, tokens/sec=12.6k, QA_acc=91.3%
INT8-GPTQ on H100 (vector-lane-v2): p95=98ms, tokens/sec=18.4k, QA_acc=89.5%
INT8-AWQ on H100: p95=115ms (high p99 jitter), tokens/sec=20.1k, QA_acc=87.1%
FP8-experimental on L4: p95=160ms, tokens/sec=11.7k, QA_acc=90.4%
A100-INT8-GPTQ (cuBLAS-fallback enabled): p95=102ms, tokens/sec=15.8k, QA_acc=89.6%
Notes: these are median-run numbers; p99 spikes can be 2-3x p95 in bad configs.
Interpretation and decision guidance:
- For latency-sensitive short-chat routes, prefer INT8-GPTQ with vector-lane-v2 on H100 but gate AWQ until prompt-sensitivity evals pass.
- For long-context customers, keep FP16 baseline as default on A100 unless FP8 shows consistent quality parity on a per-customer eval.
- Implement kernel-level automatic fallback: if p95 jumps >30% or sustained p99>target for 3 consecutive windows, switch to cuBLAS-fallback or FP16 variant for that host and emit alert.
- Add probabilistic canary: route 3% traffic to quant-variant with increased telemetry for 48 hours before enabling at 25%.
Action items:
1) Create an automated grade-check job in CI that runs the harness for short-chat & summarization (owner: Rajiv, due: 2027-06-20).
2) Add a deterministic QA prompt set for numeric reasoning (owner: Sienna, due: 2027-06-18) — required for AWQ gating.
3) Implement fallback rule in control plane: p95>baseline*1.3 => auto-fallback to FP16 for 10 minutes + Pager (owner: Ethan, PR #7821).
4) Expand testbed to include cloud GPU family L4x2 tests and add memory fragmentation tracing in runtime (owner: Maya, due: 2027-07-01).
5) Publish a short internal one-pager for GTM describing performance vs cost tradeoffs for common customer archetypes (owner: Product).
Risk notes:
- Low-signal QA checks with small prompt sets can under- or over-estimate human-perceived quality; we need to increase sample diversity.
- Driver/firmware differences across cloud providers cause non-deterministic performance — validate on target provider before customer rollout.
- Enabling automatic fallbacks can mask a deeper regression; fallback logs must be searchable and tied to deployment/commit metadata.
Appendix - quick checklist for an ad-hoc:
- Re-run short-chat harness with bursty arrival pattern (10s high qps for 2 mins).
- Check kernel telemetry: occupancy, SM utilization, and memcpy stalls.
- If p95 increases but throughput remains high, enable cuBLAS-fallback for 5 hosts and monitor.
- If QA_acc drops >2 points, pause traffic to the quant variant and open an incident.
- Record full GPU traces and upload to /bench-results for triage.
closing: Questions / comments welcome in the PR or the Confluence page. This playbook should evolve as we add more kernels and accelerator targets; please add test cases that reflect your customer workloads before approving a rollout.
